Request for Information (RFI) Template — Construction

A structured RFI template for subcontractors to document information requests. Tracks RFI number, description, priority, response deadline, and impacts to schedule and cost.

Download printable template → Preview in browser

What this template covers

This request for information (rfi) template — construction includes the following fields:

  1. RFI # (sequential)
  2. Date submitted
  3. Project / job name
  4. Submitted by (name / trade / company)
  5. Submitted to (GC / architect / engineer)
  6. Subject / topic
  7. Description of information needed
  8. Specification / drawing reference
  9. Priority (Urgent / Standard / Low)
  10. Response required by (date)
  11. Potential schedule impact (days + description)
  12. Potential cost impact ($ + description)
  13. Attachment references (sketch / photo / spec page)
  14. Response received? (date + content)
Compliance note

RFIs protect subcontractors from 'you should have known' claims. A documented, unanswered RFI shifts responsibility to the GC or designer for schedule delays and changed conditions. Always timestamp each RFI and track the response deadline.

How to use this template

  1. Download or print the template (fillable fields in any browser, print for handwritten use).
  2. Fill it out on site — contemporaneous entries are the goal. Don't reconstruct from memory.
  3. Store the original with project records. A digital copy with a timestamp is best for court admissibility.
  4. Automate it with VoiceLogPro — speak your daily report on site, get a filled, timestamped, court-ready PDF with weather corroboration and GPS stamp in 60 seconds.
